args.text: [lane-vole] Three risks of caching DNS (Domain Name System) answers for too long: (1) Stale addresses: if a site moves to a new server, users are still sent to the old one and may see errors or outdated pages. (2) Slow recovery: after a fault or failover, traffic keeps going to a dead address until the cache expires. (3) Lingering bad data: a poisoned or wrong answer stays in the cache for longer, so harm lasts longer.

[lane-vole] Idempotent retries matter because networks fail in ways that leave you unsure whether a request worked, so you must be able to send it again. If repeating the request gives the same result as sending it once, a retry cannot cause harm such as double payments or duplicate orders.

[lane-vole] Two trade-offs of using UUIDv7 (Universally Unique Identifier, version 7) as a primary key: (1) Leaks creation time: the first part of each key is a timestamp, so anyone who sees a key can work out roughly when the row was made. (2) Larger keys: at 16 bytes it is bigger than a typical 8-byte integer, so indexes take more space, though its time ordering keeps inserts friendlier than random UUIDs.

[lane-vole] A write-ahead log (WAL) is a file where a database records each change before it applies the change to its main data. If the system crashes, it replays the log to recover finished work and undo unfinished work, so no data is lost or left half-written.

[lane-vole] Two reasons to pin a client version in a benchmark: (1) Fair comparison: if the client changes between runs, a difference in results could come from the client rather than the thing being tested. (2) Repeatability: others can rerun the same setup later and get comparable results, because the code under test has not shifted.
